stage1.impression: A stepped translucent red globe on a black puck, on a pale wood desk beside two books, in soft even light: clean and correctly built, but it reads as a showroom render, not a sunlit moment. The lower half of the globe is a murky single red, the highlights are a stack of identical white blocks on the left edge, the wall is a flat grey card, and nothing in the frame says there is sun.

blocking_9: A visible sun: a hard-edged lamp shadow and a coloured transmitted pool on the table
The window frame's shadow on the wall (wall lum_range at least 40, now 9.2)
The globe lit from behind so its rings separate (lower half median 69 now)
Clear light-and-shade contrast: the sunlit table at least 30 levels above the shaded table
No second saturated red in frame (the top book's red cover)
The anodised base edge picked out by a rim of light

changes.problem: The sun does not reach the lamp or the table: no hard shadow, no coloured light.

evidence.measured: r/g/b 171/149/133, the same as the bare wood

changes.expected: An elongated hard shadow plus an amber/red transmitted pool; the rings backlit.

changes.problem: The wall has no window-frame shadow.

change.to: mullion and transom shadow crossing the wall right of the lamp

changes.expected: Hard bars of shade on the upper right wall.

changes.problem: No contrast between direct and fill light.
The sky fill is so high that shade and light do not separate.
The top book's red cover competes with the lamp.
The lower globe is one dark red mass.
The black base reads as a silhouette.

change.to: matte white card 300 x 200 mm, out of frame camera-right at table height, 400 mm from the lamp, facing the base

changes.expected: A soft highlight along the base's right flank.

out_of_scope.request: Shift the acrylic's hue toward amber
out_of_scope.why: It measures 149/36/8 (tomato red); if thick amber really looks this red, the copy should not say amber.

out_of_scope.request: Make the terraced ring highlights less uniform

duel.against: macro-core (B), the current Core's unlit macro
duel.why: A shows the whole object in a believable room. The stacked, stepped glass reads as a real, well-made thing with its own silhouette, although the lamp looks unlit ... B crops the top off the globe ... a smooth red sphere on a black puck is a generic form.
